object_description: elongated school volume within a three-garden urban composition
design_condition: The school is placed at the intersection of new residential alleys, with its surrounding buildings defining three distinct gardens while leaving the school’s routes and clearances somewhat imprecise.

positive.statement: The simple composition of streets and squares creates a true extension of the existing city.
The complementary gardens offer varied uses, atmospheres, and differentiated environments for flora and fauna.
The parking volume is tempered by its association with a built frontage and its roof gardens contribute to socialization and biodiversity.
The housing volumes allow varied forms of housing and can be divided into complementary operations or programs.
The distribution of the program enables efficient and adaptable phasing.
The school delicately asserts itself in the urban composition and its ground-floor overhangs reinforce its presence.
The structural system offers a certain adaptability of the plan over time.
The classroom orientation toward the quiet side is adapted to the work and comfort of schoolchildren.

negative.statement: The vision is unlikely to implement the municipal master planning.
The division of the green spaces does not create a true public park at the desired local scale.
The school’s location is imprecise in relation to routes crossing the block and the clearances it generates.
The school struggles to convince as a generous reference space for the establishment.
The isolation of one class from the others on each level is problematic in practice.
The covered courtyards are hardly suitable for their main destination.
